questions.prompt: When using a cloud-based LLM API in an enterprise, what is the primary compliance concern about prompt content?

choices.text: Keeping prompts short enough to avoid unexpected usage fees.
Avoiding transmission of sensitive or regulated data without approval.
Ensuring the provider does not change the model version unexpectedly.
Selecting a region primarily to minimize end-user latency.

questions.officialRationale: Privacy and regulatory obligations often restrict sending certain data (e.g., personal, health, or confidential business information) to third parties. The key compliance question is whether the organization is permitted to transmit that data and how it is protected. The other options are operational considerations, not the core compliance issue.

questions.prompt: How can context engineering help support compliance with regulations such as GDPR or HIPAA?

choices.text: By treating compliance as separate from prompt and context design.
By permanently storing complete user inputs in prompt history.
By filtering, minimizing, or masking identifiers when they are unnecessary.
By inserting the full regulation text into every model response.

questions.officialRationale: Context engineering can reduce exposure by removing or masking identifiers and restricting what the model sees. It can also shape refusal behavior for disallowed requests. Compliance also involves organizational controls, but prompt and context design directly affect privacy risk.

questions.prompt: What is a practical way to enforce a company’s brand or policy guidelines in model outputs?

choices.text: Training a new model from scratch specifically for the company voice.
Assuming the model already knows the company’s internal policies.
Requiring a person to rewrite every response before it is used.
Including the guidelines as explicit rules in the system instructions.

questions.officialRationale: System instructions are the most direct way to apply style and policy constraints consistently. Training from scratch is rarely practical, relying on general training is unreliable, and manual rewrites do not scale.

questions.prompt: Why is a human review or approval step sometimes required for AI-generated outputs in an enterprise?

choices.text: To slow delivery so users have more time to read carefully.
To prevent sensitive, incorrect, or policy-violating content from being released.
Because AI systems are always prohibited from operating without humans.
Because strong prompts remove the need for any oversight.

questions.officialRationale: Human-in-the-loop controls reduce risk when mistakes are costly or when policies require oversight. A well-designed prompt helps, but it does not eliminate the possibility of errors, unsafe content, or compliance violations.

questions.prompt: What does “model drift” mean in a deployed AI system, and why can it affect prompt performance?

choices.text: The model steadily improves on your tasks simply through usage.
The model is moved to different hardware and becomes faster.
The model’s behavior changes over time, altering how prompts are interpreted.
Prompt performance remains stable as long as your prompt text is unchanged.

questions.officialRationale: Model behavior can change due to vendor updates, configuration changes, or shifts in user inputs. A prompt tuned for one behavior can underperform later, so drift requires monitoring and periodic re-evaluation.

questions.prompt: Why should prompts and context assembly rules be version-controlled in an enterprise setting?

choices.text: To rotate prompts every day as a default security practice.
Because prompts automatically become legally binding documents.
Because prompts are one-time text that does not require maintenance.
To track changes, document reasons, and enable safe rollback when needed.

questions.officialRationale: Version control provides traceability, supports collaboration, and enables rollback if a change harms quality or compliance. Prompts and context rules should be managed like other production assets.

questions.prompt: When deploying a context-engineered solution at scale, what is a key performance consideration?

choices.text: Ensuring each user receives a unique prompt version by default.
Managing token overhead from large contexts that increases latency and cost.
Avoiding too many requests because the model becomes fatigued over time.
Using the most expensive model for every request to guarantee quality.

questions.officialRationale: Large contexts increase tokens and often increase response time and cost. Efficient context selection, caching, summarization, and routing strategies help maintain performance and affordability.

questions.prompt: How can enterprises mitigate the risk of prompt injection attacks?

choices.text: Accepting that prompt injection cannot be reduced in practice.
Relying on secrecy, so users do not know a system prompt exists.
Sanitizing and separating untrusted input, plus enforcing policy and validation.
Depending on user agreements alone to prevent malicious behavior.

questions.officialRationale: Mitigation combines handling untrusted text safely, enforcing instruction hierarchy, limiting tools, and validating outputs. Secrecy and agreements are not sufficient defenses on their own.

questions.prompt: Why must generative AI outputs be checked for compliance and bias in enterprise use?

choices.text: Large models do not require compliance review once deployed.
AI outputs are automatically treated as legal documents by regulators.
The only goal is avoiding negative publicity, not risk reduction.
The organization remains responsible for what the system communicates.

questions.officialRationale: Enterprises are accountable for the content they publish or act on. Checking for compliance, privacy, and bias reduces legal, ethical, and operational risk.

questions.prompt: What is a sensible approach to deploying a new AI assistant feature in an enterprise?

choices.text: Deploying to all users immediately to maximize early feedback.
Starting with a controlled pilot or limited rollout and expanding gradually.
Delaying release until the system is perfect under all conditions.
Releasing without notifying users to avoid changing their behavior.

questions.officialRationale: A phased rollout limits blast radius, supports learning, and allows fixes before broad exposure. Full deployment on day one is risky, and waiting for perfection prevents real-world learning.

questions.prompt: What documentation or process should accompany a deployed context-engineered AI solution?

choices.text: Only a date-stamped list of prompt versions without supporting detail.
No documentation, to keep the prompt confidential within the organization.
Documentation of intended behavior, limits, failure modes, and governance.
A screenshot of the prompt as the primary long-term record.

questions.officialRationale: Documentation supports audits, maintenance, safe updates, and cross-functional review. It should describe how the system is intended to behave and where it is known to be limited.

questions.prompt: How can compliance requirements influence the choice between a third-party LLM API and an on-prem or private deployment?

choices.text: On-prem deployments cannot meet compliance requirements in practice.
Compliance does not affect deployment choice; only cost matters.
Using a third-party API transfers all compliance responsibility to the provider.
Highly sensitive data may require on-prem or private hosting with stricter controls.

questions.officialRationale: Data residency, retention, and exposure constraints can require deployments where the organization maintains tighter control. Third-party use can be compliant, but it does not automatically remove the organization’s responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What monitoring should be in place after deploying a generative AI system in production?

choices.text: No monitoring is needed once initial testing is complete.
Logging plus routine reviews, alerts, and follow-up actions for quality and risk.
Only uptime monitoring, because content quality is not measurable.
Mandatory real-time human approval of every output, regardless of risk.

questions.officialRationale: Production systems require both technical monitoring and output monitoring (quality, policy compliance, safety, and privacy). Most organizations use risk-based sampling and targeted approvals rather than approving every response.

questions.prompt: Why is cross-functional involvement important when deploying enterprise AI solutions?

choices.text: To distribute blame across more teams if an issue occurs.
Because AI teams alone can cover legal, security, and domain risk.
Because deployment spans legal, security, operations, and domain correctness.
Because more stakeholders always improves speed of delivery.

questions.officialRationale: Enterprise AI touches legal obligations, security posture, operational stability, and domain accuracy. Cross-functional participation improves safety and compliance and reduces blind spots.

questions.prompt: When updating prompts or context strategy after deployment, what best practice helps maintain stability?

choices.text: Updating only when the vendor forces a model change.
Pushing changes directly to production to observe live behavior.
Avoiding prompt updates after launch to reduce operational complexity.
Testing updates in staging with regressions before controlled rollout.

questions.officialRationale: Treat prompt and context changes like production releases: test first, roll out gradually, and monitor key metrics with a rollback plan.
